conceptZh: 一隻高高的玩具長頸鹿和一台矮矮的小機器人想一起拍合照，第一次長頸鹿的頭出了畫面，第二次機器人整個被擋住；最後長頸鹿乾脆整隻趴下來，兩個人臉貼臉終於剛剛好。
object: a tall toy giraffe, a short toy robot and a tiny tripod camera
morph: the glyph 高 stands still as a solid sculpture while the mismatched pair try to fit into one photo
creativeAngle: 用拍照框不進去把高矮差距變成看得見的問題，三次嘗試的節奏很清楚，結尾長頸鹿趴下來遷就朋友也很可愛。高十畫、上中下三段堆疊，中間兩個口最容易畫糊，字體靜止並要求各段分明。語音詞「高手」，手ㄕㄡˇ已學過，兩字都是單一讀音。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale cream background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 高 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep teal blue, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the small top stroke and dot, the 口 beneath them, and the lower section with its own 口 inside stay clearly separated as three stacked bands, none of them merging. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. Along its base a tall toy giraffe and a short boxy toy robot shuffle together in front of a tiny tripod camera, getting ready for a photo. At 1.0 second they pose: the giraffe's head is entirely out of frame above, leaving only legs and neck. They regroup. At 1.9 seconds the giraffe crouches to help and now its body completely hides the robot, whose small hand waves helplessly from behind a knee. They regroup again, both looking at the camera for guidance. Beat. At 2.9 seconds the giraffe simply lies all the way down on its belly and rests its chin on the floor, and the robot trots over and presses his cheek right beside it - and at last the two faces sit side by side, exactly the same height, both beaming. They hold the pose happily until 4.4 seconds, then amble out of frame to the left with the tripod. From 4.7 seconds to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 高 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「高、高、高手」, using the reading ㄍㄠ for 高 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 高 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 高手 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 高: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 橡膠恐龍短手搆不到高處的積木，只好踩著越疊越高的盒子，最後疊出「高」。
object: rubber dinosaur with tiny arms, stacking boxes
morph: stacked boxes form the roof dot, a lid, and the boxes of 高
creativeAngle: 小手搆不到，叫道具一層層疊高。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy, locked frontal camera. Setting: a sky-blue backdrop with a sandy floor; the glyph is made of violet toy boxes: a top dot, a wide lid bar, and a stacked mouth-shaped frame below. A rubber dinosaur with enormous feet and tiny arms stands at left. The Traditional Chinese glyph 高 stays centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the dino stretches both tiny arms toward a top box and cannot reach it, feet stomping once; the first 高 is spoken as it jumps in vain. Moment two (1.8-3.5s): it kicks a box bar into place, hops up on it, then the whole pile wobbles; boxes fall into the exact 高 arrangement, ending in a tall tower on the right; the second 高 is spoken as the top dot lands. Moment three (3.5-5.0s): a small toy mountain with a snowy tip rises behind the dino, which spreads its tiny arms toward it; 高山 is spoken as the peak pops up. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 高 is perfectly still and unobstructed; the dino rocks proudly on its big feet and gives a tiny arm wave; the glyph is still. Voice: a gentle off-screen narrator in Taiwanese Mandarin pronounces exactly 「高、高、高山」 with Zhuyin ㄍㄠ、ㄍㄠ、ㄍㄠ ㄕㄢ, slowly and distinctly, tones clear. Timing: first utterance at about 0.5s, second at about 2.6s, the word at about 4.4s; then stop, no repeats and no extra speech. Beneath the voice only thumps and wooden clacks, no music. The single glyph is the only on-screen text; the vocabulary stays audio-only with no subtitles, watermark, clutter or flashing.

conceptZh: 拼裝玩具機器人想爬上一座高高的積木塔頂，第一次跳太用力整個飛出畫面摔成餅；第二次後仰蓄力、全速衝鋒撞塔，咚！積木嘩啦落下排成「高」，花生頭頂的小積木正好掉成最上面那一點，最後遠處小高山冒出來，機器人伸長手臂指著它。
object: a boxy toy robot with one long arm, a towering block tower, Peanut the raccoon with his wobbly stack, and a small pop-up toy mountain
morph: the robot's charge-and-crash into the tall block tower shakes the blocks loose; they rain down and land as the strokes of 高, with the top dot supplied by the top block of Peanut's stack
creativeAngle: 前兩版是合照笑話和恐龍疊盒子，這版改成「衝鋒撞牆」的大動作鬧劇：機器人馬達太強是笑點核心（先跳過頭、再撞扁），撞擊本身震落積木組成字，花生的高疊物只貢獻最上面那一點，角色不超過三個、動線由左到右一眼看懂。詞選 高山 而非 高興，因 興 為多音字，山 只有一種讀法最安全，且可用小山冒出來做具體畫面。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy comedy in one locked-off frontal shot on a clean pale butter-yellow background with a flat matte floor and nothing else behind. Only three things ever share the frame: the lead, a tall tower of chunky building blocks, and a small cartoon raccoon sidekick. The lead is a boxy toy robot assembled from mismatched parts, one arm clearly longer than the other, with round lamp eyes and motors that always run a little too strong, so every move overshoots. The tower stands center frame, built from saturated deep crimson blocks, reaching almost to the top edge. Beside it stands Peanut, a plump cartoon raccoon in a tiny vest, hugging a wobbling column of small crimson blocks far taller than himself, eyes peeking around the side.

0.0 to 1.5 seconds: the robot stands at far left, spots the tower top, and its lamp eyes go wide; it stretches the long arm straight up and points at the summit, hopping once with excitement, motors whirring. The off-screen voice says the first 高 at about 0.6 seconds exactly as the long arm points high.

1.5 to 3.0 seconds: first try. The robot bends its knees and leaps for the top, but the motors fire too hard; it rockets straight up and out of frame, a beat of empty air, then drops back down flat on its face at the tower's foot with a soft clank, squashed thin like a pancake. It pops back up to shape, shakes its head, and glares at the tower. Peanut salutes it crisply at exactly the wrong moment, and his stack sways.

3.0 to 4.6 seconds: the big one. The robot backs up to the far left, digs both feet into the floor, leans so far back it almost tips over in a huge cartoon wind-up, motors revving louder, a frozen beat of anticipation, then charges full speed left to right and slams into the tower base with a big squashy BONK. The robot compresses like an accordion against the blocks. The impact shakes the whole tower loose and the blocks rain down, landing one by one with soft wooden clacks in the exact arrangement of the Traditional Chinese character 高: a short horizontal bar near the top, below it a small square 口, and beneath that a taller rectangular frame 冂 with its own small 口 sitting inside, all three parts clearly separated and stacked vertically in standard textbook proportions. At the very end of the fall Peanut's stack tips and its topmost tiny block drops neatly into position as the single dot above the top bar. The voice says the second 高 at about 4.3 seconds, right as the final blocks click into place. The finished glyph is centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with comfortable margins, in solid saturated crimson against the pale background.

4.6 to 8.0 seconds: the glyph stays perfectly still and untouched for the rest of the clip. The robot peels off the blocks flattened like a sheet of paper, wobbles two dizzy steps to the lower left with a wide goofy grin and spinning lamp eyes, then a hiccup pops it back to its boxy shape. At about 5.3 seconds a small toy mountain with a snowy white cap pops up in the lower right margin, well clear of the glyph, and the voice says 高山 exactly as the peak springs into view; the robot swings its long arm to point at the mountain and nods proudly while Peanut salutes the mountain instead of the robot. For the remaining hold the robot does a tiny proud sway and Peanut gathers his fallen blocks, both staying away from the strokes and never covering them.

Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft even studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts, no motion blur on the glyph. Cartoon squash-and-stretch on the robot only; the blocks land crisp and solid.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin with Taiwan standard readings and says exactly 「高、高、高山」(ㄍㄠ、ㄍㄠ、ㄍㄠ ㄕㄢ), reading precisely those syllables slowly and distinctly with clear tones: the first 高 at about 0.6 seconds, the second 高 at about 4.3 seconds, and 高山 at about 5.3 seconds while the finished glyph is still on screen, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. Beneath the voice only soft motor whirs, a gentle cartoon bonk and light wooden clacks, no music louder than the voice, no loud startling sounds. The single character 高 is the only text anywhere in the frame; the vocabulary word is audio only, with no subtitles, no other letters or numbers, no watermark, no extra props, no particles, no lens flare and no flashing effects.
